title: Bound OCI directory index traversal depth
description: The independent F4.3 audit noted that path depth is capped, but directory index pages are recursively followed without an explicit structural-depth cap. A registry containing a very long, acyclic chain of valid one-child branch indexes can cause excessive network requests and recursive stack/work during lookup or mutation. Add a maximum directory-page depth or iterative traversal, and fail closed with a typed integrity/resource-limit error.
acceptance_criteria: Valid trees within the documented bound continue to read and mutate. A real or narrowly constructed adversarial OCI index chain exceeding the bound is rejected without stack overflow or unbounded requests. Document the limit and keep writer output within it.
notes: Non-blocking finding from independent audit of revision 813b66a3696304ed105c689be48b22ceaa38d894 (reviewer agent c8e29c52-1277-492). Ordinary writer-produced trees and current 129-entry tests are unaffected; this is registry-controlled structure hardening.

title: Prove graceful shutdown drains an in-flight HTTP request
description: The F1.3 independent audit found the current subprocess test sends SIGTERM only after all requests finish, so it verifies the signal and exit path but not draining active work. Add black-box coverage once a legitimate route or injectable handler can provide a deterministic delayed response. Do not add a production-only test backdoor solely for this assertion. Verify SIGTERM stops accepting new requests while an already active request either completes before process exit or follows an explicitly documented cancellation contract.
acceptance_criteria: A subprocess test holds an actual HTTP request in flight, sends SIGTERM, and asserts the documented drain/cancellation behavior and process exit. The test uses a real listener, is deterministic, runs in cargo test, and introduces no secret or local artifact persistence.
